pretreatment: baked overnight by heating the sample pedestal to 868 K (corresponding to a sample temperature of 650 K) and the chamber walls to about 393 K
evidence: Samples 17 /C217 mm were cut from 10-nm-thick SiO 2/Si(100) wafer material. Once installed, puck position could be manipulated by a linear motion feedthrough, and the temperature raised by a tungsten filament. A type-K thermocouple mounted in the pedestal was connected to a proportional-integral-derivative temperature controller, which was interfaced with a DC-power supply to control the tungsten filament current. The sample temperature was determined from a correlation of the pedestal thermocouple output with that of a thermocouple mounted on the sample surface of a calibration wafer. This was also checked against the melting point of In wire (430 K) and 63/37 lead-tin solder (453 K) placed on the sample surface.
